title: Reports on Every Hand-Over
eyebrow: The wall is up: no agent can tick anything off, or ask you anything, without a current page

actions.fyi: You answered the one question this page had, and the next-up line at the top of every report now says what the agent is about to do. An outside reader went over the whole thing afterwards and found nine points; eight were real and are fixed — the worst of them meant that you opening a page cleared the very refusal it exists to make.

content.label: What changed for you
content.lead: Until today you got told about work when an agent decided it was worth telling you about.

rows: An agent ticks something off your list
A page, and the link in chat
A question in chat, on its own
The question with what it costs behind it

One page per piece of work, and on its card

blocks.label: Measured before designing anything
blocks.text: Across every session this project has ever run: 16829 turns changed a file, and not one of them handed you a link. This is not agents forgetting. Nothing has ever asked them.

blocks.label: The two faults you ran into are gone
blocks.text: The button on a card was sending the report somewhere with no work list in it, so it opened an error instead of a page. It now opens. A button with nowhere to build a page no longer appears at all, since it could only ever open an error. And a report written while working in a side copy was filing itself under that copy's throwaway name; it now files under the project.

blocks.label: Your checklist reads in order now
blocks.text: It was sorted by state, and the work list hands its rows back newest first, so the finished half ran one way and the unfinished half ran the other. The list is now simply the order the work happened in, with the ticks falling where they fell. Two more things it was getting wrong: work written and waiting to merge, and work waiting on your signature, both showed as nobody had started them; work you dropped showed as work still to do, and now leaves the list.

content.label: What fires a report, and what does not
content.lead: Two triggers, both things a machine can see without asking anyone's opinion.

rows.title: Something on your list got finished
rows.note: A piece of work, or a whole job, is ticked off. The page is brought up to date and the link goes to you as part of ticking it off — not afterwards, and not if the agent remembers.

rows.title: The agent wants your input
rows.note: Any question, any approval, any pick between two ways. The question goes on the page with what each answer costs, and the chat line is the question itself so you can answer where you are.

rows.title: Not: working, reading, answering you
rows.note: Turns spent building something owe nothing until the thing is finished. Neither does reading code, searching, answering a question of yours, or bookkeeping. You narrowed this yourself, and it is what keeps the pages worth opening.

content.label: Why your last word mattered so much
content.lead: It moved the rule off the one place in the machinery that cannot hold anything.

blocks.label: A refusal at the end of a turn is worth exactly one push
blocks.text: When a check refuses to let an agent finish, the harness lets it try again — and if the same check refuses a second time, the harness overrules the check and lets the agent stop anyway. That is deliberate, so a broken check cannot trap a session forever. Anything built on that refusal can nudge an agent once and never more.

rows.title: Tying it to finishing a piece of work moves it somewhere that holds
rows.note: Ticking something off your list is an action the agent has to ask the machinery for, and the machinery can simply say no — with no limit and no second chance. So the report is not owed after the work is finished; it is part of finishing it. An agent with no page cannot tick anything off, which is the wall you asked for.

rows.title: The same wall carries the question half
rows.note: Putting a question to you is also something the agent has to ask for, and it is refused the same way. No page, no question. Both halves are now absolute rather than one absolute and one hopeful.

rows.title: The one soft edge left, named honestly
rows.note: The machinery can make sure the page exists and is current. Whether the link actually reaches your chat is the one part it can only push once. In practice the page is already written by then and pasting a link is nothing, so this is a nudge on the cheapest possible act — but it is a nudge, not a wall, and you should know which is which.

content.label: Why your pages read as out of date
content.lead: You said it of every report, not just one, and you are right about the cause.

rows.title: The two lines at the top can only ever repeat the work list
rows.note: Now and next-up are worked out from the state of each row on your list and nothing else. If the agent has not ticked its rows off, the page says nothing has started — even where the thing is built and measured lower down the same page. That is the fog page you showed me: built, measured, and reading as not started.

rows.title: Next-up names a stage, not a thing
rows.note: It picks the first row nobody has started, and for a job in the middle of building that row is called "Build it". Useless to you. Meanwhile the agent has written what actually happens next — fog pictures, in that case — into the page's own plan at the bottom, where you have to scroll to find it.

rows.title: What I would change, if you say so
rows.note: Take the next-up line from what the agent wrote, and leave the tick list as the work list's own answer. Then the top of the page says what is about to happen in the agent's words, and the list underneath stays something you can hold them to. The question is at the top of this page.

rows.title: The half that is already fixed either way
rows.note: The refusal that went in today means an agent cannot tick a row off while its page is behind the work — so from now on a page and its list move together. It does not fix the pages of jobs that went stale before today.

content.label: What the outside reader found
content.lead: One round, by an agent that did not write any of it. Nine points; eight were real and are fixed.

blocks.label: The one that mattered
blocks.text: Opening a report in the browser rebuilt it, and the wall was watching the rebuilt page. So you looking at a page would have quietly cleared the very refusal it exists to make. It now watches what an agent writes, which no amount of looking can touch.

rows.title: A plan could never have been handed over
rows.note: Presenting a plan was refused until a page existed, but the mode an agent plans in forbids writing files — so the page could not be written. It was a trap with no way out. Plans are back to being handed over the ordinary way.

rows.title: Any page would open the door
rows.note: A question was allowed as long as some page somewhere had been written, including another project's or another agent's. It now has to be a page of this project, carrying work this agent holds.

rows.title: Two more holes and two loose ends
rows.note: Trimming the conversation mid-turn forgave every refusal that turn had earned; the two halves disagreed about which cards owe you anything; the Reports button on your toolbar still opened an error where the card button had learned not to; and dropped work reached your checklist as a finished tick.

rows.title: The one I answered rather than fixed
rows.note: It asked for a test suite for the refusals. You ruled twice today that the board is not tested in this project, because a suite has to create work on your board to have something to refuse. So they are proved by being fired at real cards instead — which is how every point above was checked.

rows.title: Finishing something takes a little longer
rows.note: An agent that would have ticked an item off and moved on now brings its page up to date first. Everything between stays as fast as it is today — your narrowing took this from a tax on every turn to a tax on every finish.

rows.title: You will get the same link several times over a job
rows.note: A job with several pieces in it pings you once per piece, always on the same link, each time opening a page that has moved on. Enough to catch an agent going the wrong way early; not so much that the link becomes noise you stop clicking.

rows.title: The half that reads the board is free
rows.note: The tick list on every page is the work list's own answer, so nobody writes it and it cannot drift. Only the words and pictures cost anything.

rows.title: The risk worth naming
rows.note: An agent that cannot write a page cannot finish anything, so a fault in the report machinery stops all work rather than just going unreported. Two things already found and waiting to be fixed first are exactly that kind of fault.

decisions.title: One page per piece of work, updated in place
decisions.why: A new page per hand-over buries the current state under history. Same page, same decision numbers, always current — which is also why the tenth ping costs you nothing to read.

decisions.title: A card is where the report also shows, never what fires it
decisions.why: You asked for a report every step of the way, not on the board's schedule. Work with no card behind it owes you a page just the same.

decisions.title: Bookkeeping is not a piece of work
decisions.why: Claiming a card, setting up a workspace and writing notes change things without producing anything you would want to read. Counting them would bury the hand-overs that matter.

decisions.title: Helpers an agent sends off owe nothing
decisions.why: They hand their answer back to the agent that sent them, not to you. The agent that talks to you is the one that owes you the page.

decisions.title: The rule is held here, and written down where every project can read it
decisions.why: The report tools are already shared across projects; only this one has the machinery to refuse. Another project inherits the rule the day it adopts that machinery.

decisions.title: When the page exists to ask you something, the chat line is the question itself
decisions.why: You answer in the terminal. Making you open a page to find out what is being asked adds a click to every decision you make.

decisions.title: A piece of work means one your list says is finished, not a turn that changed a file
decisions.why: Your words: work is only when it completed a task, subtask or step on the list. It is cheaper for you to read, cheaper for an agent to produce, and it is the only version that can be held absolutely.

decisions.title: The page is part of finishing something, not a debt owed afterwards
decisions.why: You asked that an agent owing a report cannot take its next move. Refusing the finish itself is that rule with no way round it: the item stays open, the job stays open, and nothing after it can start.

decisions.title: No page, no question
decisions.why: Your words. An agent that wants your input hands you the page carrying it first, so every question you answer arrives with what it costs already attached.

decisions.title: A report button with nowhere to build its page is not shown
decisions.why: It could only ever open an error, which is what you hit. Nothing there says truthfully that this card has no report you can open from here; a button that fails says something false.

decisions.title: Work you dropped leaves the checklist
decisions.why: It was showing as work still to do, which is the opposite of what dropping it meant. It is not finished either, so there is no honest tick for it — it simply is not on the list.

decisions.title: The refusals stand aside for something merely noticed, a question, or a ruling you made
decisions.why: Nothing was finished on those, so there is nothing to tell you about. Every other card owes a page, including ones whose work lands in another repository.

next.if_nothing: The wall stays up and the rest of this job finishes without you.

steps.step: Every agent on this project is held to the wall from its next session
